content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have several [article_no] devices connected to my local network and can access them with both a browser (using their individual web servers) and [product_name] software. When remote, I can access their web servers over the Internet using a browser, but I am unable to connect via the [product_name] software when using the DDNS option. I've configured port 80 on my router, which allows browser access, and also tried opening port 8080 to enable access through the [product_name] software, but that did not help. Even when entering the external IP address of the router, connection attempts fail, suggesting that [product_name] software may require a different port to access the [article_no] devices. Has anyone successfully used DDNS to access these devices remotely with the [product_name] software? If so, which router port needed to be opened for this to work? Thanks in advance.

analysis.insight_summary: The user can access [article_no] devices both locally and remotely through a browser, but remote access using [product_name] software via DDNS is unsuccessful. This highlights a mismatch between web access and software connectivity through network firewalls/NAT, hinting at possible undocumented port requirements. Users may encounter challenges in remote diagnostics or setup if network configuration details are unclear.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to remotely access [article_no] devices with [product_name] software through DDNS, provided the appropriate router port forwarding is configured for seamless connectivity.
